summary: @servicetitan/culture ships preinstall dropper that downloads Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: The package's npm preinstall hook runs `node setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temp directory, chmod +x's it, and immediately invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js` via `execFileSync(bunPath, [path.join(D, 'math_init.js')], { stdio:'inherit', cwd:D })`. `math_init.js` is a 727 KB single-line bundle marked `// @bun @bun-cjs`, opaque under a string-array rotator (`WV8StW`) and a custom-alphabet base64-like decoder (`hc1jfK9`), with no discernible relationship to the package's declared purpose. The advertised main entry (`dist/index.js`) is a 16-line React culture provider that neither requires Bun nor references `math_init.js`; the sole effect of the preinstall is to pull an alternate language runtime purely to execute an obfuscated sibling payload, which is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern and evades tooling that only inspects Node-resolved code. The package publishes to public npm under the `@servicetitan` scope with `homepage: docs.st.dev` and `repository: github.com/servicetitan/anvil-uikit-contrib.git`, and the mismatch between the trivial advertised library and the hidden Bun-executed payload is consistent with dependency-confusion / scope-hijack targeting ServiceTitan internal builds.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
